projects.title: Online Retail SQL Analysis
projects.description: Designed a normalized PostgreSQL database (5 tables + 1 staging table, 3NF, indexed foreign keys) for a 500,000+ row UK e-commerce transaction dataset, then wrote 30 production-ready SQL queries covering customer segmentation (RFM, LTV, cohort retention), product performance and cross-sell analysis, temporal trends, and anomaly detection using window functions (RANK, LAG, SUM OVER, NTILE, PERCENTILE_CONT), CTEs, and statistical aggregation. Surfaced that £8.91M in revenue from 4,339 customers is 82% UK-concentrated, that the top 10% of customers drive 61% of revenue, and that sub-£5 budget products generate 71% of revenue despite being a volume rather than margin business. Went further than reporting results: audited the query outputs themselves and documented real data-quality findings, including a CURRENT_DATE bug that silently mislabeled 100% of customers as "Inactive" and a cohort query that only ever returned month zero — the kind of self-auditing that separates production analysis from a one-off script.
projects.shortDescription: Designed a normalized PostgreSQL schema and wrote 30 production SQL queries analyzing 500K+ e-commerce transactions, uncovering revenue concentration and segmentation insights while auditing and documenting real bugs in the analysis itself

projects.title: Nashville Housing Market Analysis
projects.description: Engineered a raw, unstructured municipal housing dataset of 56,636 rows into a verified, stakeholder-ready business intelligence solution using advanced Excel. De-duplicated 168 exact-duplicate sales records, designed defensive null-value routing that classified 30,619 unvalued records as "N/A" instead of zero to prevent market-tier skew, and engineered derived time-dimension and boolean flag columns. Built a dynamic formula engine combining VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, and INDEX/MATCH for record retrieval with SUMIFS/COUNTIFS/AVERAGEIFS for localized statistics, and replaced standard aggregations with SUBTOTAL and SUMPRODUCT logic so every metric recalculates safely under live filters. Delivered a BI dashboard with 9 pivot tables, 5 KPI indicators, and a slicer-driven 2x3 matrix chart layout. Uncovered $18.50B in verified transaction value across 56,468 sales — a $327,581 average against a $205,838 median sale price, flagging significant high-value outlier skew — progressing from 11,338 sales ($2.78B) in 2013 to a 16,794-sale, $6.71B peak in 2015 (52% dollar-volume growth) before cooling to 14,055 sales ($4.23B) in 2016. Also surfaced ~80% capital concentration in Nashville proper and an 8.6% vacant-property sale rate — insights translated into geographic allocation, seasonal listing timing, and risk-monitoring recommendations for stakeholders.
projects.shortDescription: Transformed 56,636 messy municipal housing records (2013-2016) into a verified $18.50B market analysis — surfacing a $327,581 average vs. $205,838 median sale price to flag outlier skew — via an Excel formula engine (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/SUMPRODUCT) and a 9-pivot-table KPI dashboard

projects.title: GDHO Dataset Analysis
projects.description: Extended real-world database consulting experience gained as a contract Database Consultant at Humanitarian Outcomes (May 2023 – Dec 2025), working directly with the GDHO Airtable and database, into a full independent analysis and machine-learning pipeline on Humanitarian Outcomes' own published Global Database of Humanitarian Organisations (GDHO) 2025 release — 125,125 org-year rows across 7,301 unique humanitarian organizations (national NGOs, international NGOs, Red Cross/Crescent societies, UN agencies) tracked from 2006 to 2024. Cleaned and typed the raw export, then computed 20 statistically-backed insights covering sector composition, budget concentration, geography, and data-quality limitations: national NGOs are 81% of organizations but only 3.4% of reported budget (a ~6,780x median-budget gap to UN agencies), only ~7% of reported budgets carry an "Actual" provenance flag versus GDHO's own imputation, and hundreds of organizations share identical imputed budget figures — evidence GDHO imputes by bucket rather than per organization. Built a LightGBM budget-estimator pipeline as an independent cross-check, deliberately excluding every field derived from or co-dependent with the target to avoid leakage, and evaluated with an organization-level (not row-level) train/test split since the same organization repeats across up to 19 years — achieving a 0.796 held-out R² and 2.8% median absolute percentage error on organizations never seen in training. Documented an honest limitation: because most training labels are themselves GDHO-imputed, a meaningful share of the model's accuracy reflects re-deriving GDHO's own imputation formula rather than discovering independently verified ground truth. Delivered as a technical insights report, an ML methodology report, and a plain-language business report for non-technical stakeholders.
projects.shortDescription: Cleaned and analyzed 125,125 org-year rows covering 7,301 humanitarian organizations (GDHO 2025, 2006-2024), surfacing a 6,780x median-budget gap between national NGOs and UN agencies, then built a LightGBM budget estimator (0.796 held-out R², org-grouped train/test split) with an honest audit of its own imputation limitations

projects.title: Superstore Sales Analysis
projects.description: Performed exploratory analysis and built a 12-month sales forecast for the Superstore retail dataset (9,994 order lines, Jan 2014 - Dec 2017) across Region, Category, Sub-Category, Segment, and Ship Mode. Found that discount rate and profit margin correlate at -0.86 — unprofitable orders carry a 48% average discount versus 8% on profitable ones — and that 1,871 of 9,994 order lines (18.7%) post negative profit, giving back $156,131 total. Identified Tables as the single largest profit drag (-$17,725) despite being a top-6 product by sales volume, and Texas as the #3 state by revenue but the single biggest loss-maker (-$25,729), pointing to a discounting problem rather than a demand problem in both cases. Built a 12-month sales forecast by splitting 48 months of aggregated monthly sales into a 42-month training window and 6-month holdout, then compared Prophet against auto-ARIMA (SARIMA): Prophet won on the holdout (20.7% MAPE vs. 27.8%) and was refit on the full series to project 12 months forward, forecasting $778,333 in sales — 6.2% above the trailing 12 months — consistent with the recurring Q4 seasonal peak found in the historical data. Delivered as a full EDA and forecasting results document plus an executive-level business report.
projects.shortDescription: Analyzed 9,994 Superstore order lines (2014-2017), finding an 18.7% loss-making order rate driven by deep discounting (-0.86 margin correlation) and a $17,725 loss-making Tables sub-category, then built a Prophet vs. SARIMA sales forecast (20.7% MAPE) projecting 6.2% revenue growth over the next 12 months
